column1: # The calibration contract for autospec's live-region gate, measured against
# skills/autospec-shared/scripts/ui-liveregion-{evidence,induce}.mjs.
# This tier cannot read files; it has to drive the app. It does that two ways, and the two
# halves are listed separately below because they demand very different things of a repo.
# Run ./check-liveregions.sh.
# A rule id of "-" means no finding is expected for that state. A route line with SKIPPED
# means the route had nothing to induce.
# route[state]
# ── Induced: nothing added to these pages ────────────────────────────────────────
# No hook, no manifest entry, no test attribute. autospec holds each page's own fetch to
# watch its pending state, then releases it once normally and once as a 500. Every row here
# is produced from ordinary application code, which is the point: this half measures repos
# that have never heard of the gate.
# The reference. Announces both outcomes and clears aria-busy.
/runs.html[success]
/runs.html[error]
# Replaces the list, says nothing, and leaves aria-busy set — so even a later announcement
# would be suppressed. Sighted users see the new rows; nobody else is told.
/fixtures/live-regions/induce-silent.html[success]
/fixtures/live-regions/induce-silent.html[success]
/fixtures/live-regions/induce-silent.html[error]
# Handles success correctly and has no error path at all. The failed request produces
# nothing: no render, no message, no indication. This is the row that argues for induction
# over a manifest — nobody declares an "error" state for a failure they forgot to handle.
/fixtures/live-regions/induce-ignored.html[success]
/fixtures/live-regions/induce-ignored.html[error]
# A static page makes no data request, so there is no state to drive. Recorded as skipped
# with a reason, which is different from being checked and found clean.
/index.html
# ── Declared: states no request can produce ──────────────────────────────────────
# Form validation, optimistic updates, client-side route changes. Induction cannot reach
# these, so they are declared in .autospec/ui-test-hooks.json and driven through the hook.
/states.html[loading]
/states.html[error]
/states.html[success]
/fixtures/live-regions/inserted-with-content.html[success]
/fixtures/live-regions/silent-update.html[success]
/fixtures/live-regions/hidden-region.html[success]
/fixtures/live-regions/stuck-busy.html[success]
/fixtures/live-regions/shouted-status.html[success]
/fixtures/live-regions/no-hook.html[success]
/fixtures/live-regions/inert-hook.html[success]
# TEST_HOOK_FAILED needs no fixture of its own: states.html already throws on a state name
# it does not know, so a manifest carrying a typo produces it exactly as a real one would.
/states.html[sucess]
# Carried inside fixtures rather than as rows, because each assertion is an absence:
#   hidden-region.html    also fills an .sr-only region, hidden the correct way and still in
#                         the accessibility tree. Exactly one HIDDEN row above, not two, is
#                         what proves the gate leaves it alone.
#   states.html[loading]  leaves aria-busy set on purpose. A clean row proves the manifest's
#                         "busy": true declaration is honoured.
#   runs.html             holds aria-busy through its pending state and clears it on arrival.
#                         Two clean rows prove induction does not punish correct loading.
